title: UX-driven Observability Play Canvas: composite SLIs, trace ownership, and metric prioritization
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note frames an "UX-first" approach for observable signals: prioritize instrumentation and dashboards by direct impact to user-facing journeys rather than purely system-level metrics. The aim is a compact set of composite SLIs that map to product UX outcomes (first-token latency, meaningful-response correctness, embed-retrieval freshness) plus a practical tracing and retention policy that balances debugability with trace storage cost.

Context / Problem statement:
- We have many low-level runtime and infra metrics (gpu-util, rpc-latency, kv-eviction) but operators and product managers struggle to translate them into user-impact stories.
- Current dashboards are long lists of panels; operators take too long to form hypotheses during incidents.
- Trace retention is expensive; team needs guidelines for which requests get full span retention.

High-level approach (UX-driven):
1) Identify 3–5 critical user journeys per product area (chat generation, embeddings search, reranking). These become the canonical owners of composite SLIs.
2) For each journey, define a small set of composite SLIs (1 safety/quality SLI, 1 latency SLI, 1 freshness/accuracy SLI). Composite SLIs should be derivable from existing signals but expressible in product terms.
3) Design dashboards that surface SLI health first (top-left), then causal anchors (KV warmth, model-variant-fanout, network tails), then enrichment links (trace links, recent evals, exemplar requests).
4) Apply sampling and retention tiers for traces based on SLI status and severity.

Example composite SLI definitions (template):
- Journey: Chat-generation (token-streaming)
  - SLI_latency_first_token: percentage of requests where time-to-first-token <= 200ms at p95, evaluated over 5m window. (Derived from request.start -> first-token event)
  - SLI_generation_quality: fraction of sampled responses that pass automated quality eval (prompt-specific evals) >= 96% over 24h window. (Requires periodic automated evals)
  - SLI_hallucination_signal: percentage of moderation flags + downstream manual reports below threshold.

- Journey: Embedding-search
  - SLI_query_p99_us: p99 end-to-end latency for embedding lookup + nearest-neighbor retrieval <= 120ms
  - SLI_retrieval_freshness: percent of queries that hit index updated within last 5min >= 99%

Measurement notes:
- Whenever possible use event-driven markers (first-token emitted, final-token emitted, embedding-return) so SLI derivation is robust to container restarts and retries.
- Store SLI raw time-series at 1m resolution, derived quantiles at 5m. Keep raw for 14 days, derived aggregates for 90 days.

Tracing and sampling policy (practical):
Tier A: full-span retention (30 days)
- If a request fails an SLI (example: first-token latency breach at p95) OR triggers a high-severity user-visible error code.
- Sticky sessions flagged by product experiments (canary cohorts).
Tier B: partial spans with sparse logs (7 days)
- Random 0.5% sample of successful requests for ongoing performance profiling.
- 100% of requests flagged by feature-flagged rollouts for the rollout duration.
Tier C: ephemeral traces (48 hours)
- Low-risk background jobs, healthchecks, warmup probes.

Budgeting for trace cost:
- Estimate baseline qps * average spans per request * bytes-per-span. Convert to monthly GB and cost using our storage pricing. Use this formula each quarter to set sampling targets.
- Proposal: convert 30% of current full-span retention to Tier B (partial) by trimming low-value spans (framework internals) — preserve top-level spans and critical annotations.

Dashboard design guidance (operator-first):
- Single-pane-of-glass for each journey: 1 row = SLI overview (sparkline + current state), 2nd row = root-cause anchors (kv-warmth, model-queue-length, gpu-queue), 3rd = recent offending request samples (linked to trace viewer).
- Reduce panel count: target 6–9 panels per journey dashboard. Use drilldowns not giant pages.
- Color rules driven by SLI severity tiers rather than raw thresholds. E.g. yellow for SLI at risk (p95 crossing), red for breached SLO.

Instrumentation checklist (minimum viable):
- Markers: request.start, model.load-start, first-token, final-token, kv-read, kv-evict, model-variant, tenant-id, experiment-id.
- Service tags: short service names, request-id, tenant-id, region.
- Derived events: SLI_flag_{name}, fallback_invoked, cache_miss_count.

Ownership and rollout policy:
- Each journey must have a named owner (product or platform) and a resident SLI steward (eng team) who is responsible for dashboards and alerts.
- Rollout steps: feature flag -> smoke probe (synthetic probe per journey) -> canary -> gradual rollout with SLI watch.

Quick decision matrix: when to add full spans vs cheaper signals:
- If the expected time to diagnose using metrics/dashboards > 15 minutes AND the feature is in canary -> keep full spans.
- If operation cost per month for trace retention > 3x value in seconds-saved for oncall -> degrade to Tier B.

Next steps (action items):
- (Owners) Draft canonical journey list for hosted-api product by 2026-03-16 (owner: Priya).
- (Observability) Implement first-token and final-token markers across python + go SDKs — add span annotations for model-variant by 2026-03-23 (owner: Liam).
- (Product) Align 3 critical SLIs with PMs and set initial guardrails (owner: Diego) by 2026-03-20.

Open questions / discussion points:
- How do we integrate automated quality-evals into SLI pipelines without incurring excessive compute costs?
- What compact partial-span encoding can we standardize to preserve debug-meaning while cutting bytes?

Appendix: short glossary:
- Composite SLI: a product-facing indicator computed from multiple lower-level signals that describes user experience.
- First-token latency: time from request acceptance to emission of first token to client.
- KV warmth: percentage of requests where required context/prefix was served from fast KV cache.

End of canvas. Feedback welcome — paste comments inline or add to linked JIRA OBS-1234.
